title: parity/cmd-*.md inventories name a revision and nothing re-derives them when the source moves -- cmd-upgrade.md is right for 69d42a7 and wrong for today
body:
`intent/st/ST0056/parity/cmd-upgrade.md` is generated by `parity/tools/gen_inventory.sh` and carries its own banner: `Measured at 69d42a7 from parity/probes/toplevel.tsv. Generated by parity/tools/gen_inventory.sh -- re-run it rather than editing this file.`

IT IS RIGHT FOR ITS REVISION AND WRONG FOR TODAY. Its flag table declares `--backup-dir` and `--no-backup`, and its captured `--help` output reads `Usage: intent upgrade [--backup-dir DIR] [--no-backup]`. It declares no `--dry-run`, and that is CORRECT for `69d42a7`: `--dry-run` appears zero times in `bin/intent_upgrade` at that revision and entered at `55fc4a509`. The current twin parses it. Nothing re-derived the inventory when the source moved.

THE DEFECT IS NOT THE STALE CONTENT -- THE BANNER IS HONEST AND THE REVISION IS NAMED. The defect is that nothing triggers a re-derivation, so the staleness grows silently and its only symptom is disagreement with a hand-authored artefact that nobody is comparing it against either. This is the same class as `0250` landing on the parity apparatus itself.

IT IS A SEPARATE ROW FROM THE UPGRADE FLAG GAP, DELIBERATELY. That one's remedy is a table edit; this one's remedy is a re-derivation trigger. Filing them together would let fixing the cheaper one close the row.

REACH NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: `cmd-upgrade.md` is one member. The population is every `parity/cmd-*.md` the generator writes, and the honest first step is to measure how many of them name a revision that is no longer HEAD rather than to fix this one.

Size: S to measure the population and state it; the trigger itself is unsized until that number exists.
